driver.title: Driver app: Voltify inside a partner's app
driver.intro: Drivers install nothing new. The partner (vehicle maker, delivery company, swap network) receives Voltify's webhooks and shows the battery status and alerts in its own app. You are playing the driver: tap the phone as a driver would.
driver.phoneCaption: The partner app is a mock-up. The “Bike battery” card and the notifications use exactly what Voltify sends over the API.

driver.manualNote: The selected vehicle does not react by itself: tap “Directions” or “I have stopped” on the phone. After a fault starts, the AI needs about 15 to 25 simulated minutes to detect it (a few tens of seconds at {{speed}}×). Change the speed in the top bar.

overview.headline: Early warning of e-moped battery fire risk, right inside the app drivers already use.
overview.sub: Voltify takes battery telemetry from the vehicle maker or the fleet, its AI scores the risk and explains why, then a webhook lets the partner's app tell the driver in plain words. Fleet managers follow everything on one screen.

script: Open the Driver app: battery normal, the driver only sees battery %, km and “Normal”.
Press “Cause a fault: internal short” at 20× or 60×. When the notification appears, pause (or drop to 5×) to explain it.
Within a few tens of seconds: a push “Your battery needs a check” with the nearest swap station.
With no reaction, the risk rises to Danger: a red full-screen “Stop now”.
Open the Operations console: the incident tops the queue with its reasons and “driver notified”. Take it, call the driver, close it with a label.
Open API integration: show the customer the webhook they would receive.
honest: All data is simulated; no fleet shares real data with the team yet. This MVP is meant to win the first pilot.
On the PoC's simulated data the AI reaches 91.9% recall, 65.8% precision and a 19.3 min mean lead time; the 30 to 45 min target is not met.
Voltify does not control vehicles; the MVP only monitors and alerts. Voltify supports the BMS, it does not replace it.
Range left is an estimate (assumes 22 Wh/km).

integration.title: Integration: how a partner plugs Voltify in
integration.intro: Voltify is an API. A partner sends battery telemetry and gets incidents and driver notifications back by webhook. Everything on this page also runs on a real server (the api/ folder of the repo).
integration.source: Where this page gets its data
integration.sourceHint: By default the page simulates in the browser, so no server is needed. With `npm run dev:api` running, enter the server address and the page uses the same API a partner would (REST + Server-Sent Events).

ep.telemetry: Send telemetry (one message or a batch); vendor format detected
ep.registerVehicle: Register a vehicle, its driver and fitted pack
ep.driverView: Simplified battery status for the driver app
ep.resolve: Close an incident, label real/false alarm
ep.notificationAck: The app reports the driver tapped a notification
ep.webhooks: Subscribe a URL to events (returns the signing secret)

integration.auth: Authenticate with the x-api-key header. Webhooks carry a Voltify-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256) so partners can check they come from Voltify; failed deliveries are retried after 1, 5 and 20 seconds.
